claim: Sodium and lithium alkoxides displaced vinylic fluorine in difluorobutenolides 1 and 2 with complete regioselectivity at the beta carbon, affording products 4–10.
The authors formulate the oxyanion substitution as 1,4-addition followed by fluoride expulsion from a metal-enolate intermediate.
Under the reported conditions, the branched alkoxides examined reacted more slowly than the primary alkoxides examined.
The sodium/tert-butanol condition gave no detected conversion of butenolide 1, whereas the NaH/DME condition afforded product 9 in 53% yield.
The O-nucleophile scope included simple alkoxides, protected polyhydroxy-compound and sugar alkoxides, and substituted phenoxides; phenoxide products 14–24 were obtained in moderate to good yields.

Methyl- and phenylmagnesium bromide modified with a CuBr-dimethyl sulfide complex reacted with butenolide 1 exclusively at the beta position to give C-substituted products 25 and 26; carbonyl-addition products were not observed.
Under the reported CuBr-dimethyl sulfide-modified Grignard conditions, methyl and phenyl products 25 and 26 were isolated in 55% and 77% yield, respectively.

Methyllithium and phenyllithium followed a different reaction pathway from the modified Grignard reagents, producing rearranged compounds 27 and 28 that lacked the starting butenolide-ring carbonyl signature and contained a ketone group.

The authors propose that hemiacetal salt 30 is in equilibrium with ring-opened lithium alkoxide 31; acid quenching liberates hydroxy compounds 32 and 33, and an unstable protonated hemiacetal is proposed to rearrange to 36, which eliminates HF to give furanone 28.

Dimethyl chloromalonate, ethyl 2-chloroacetoacetate, and dimethyl malonate react with naphthoquinone derivatives mainly by vicarious nucleophilic substitution or oxidative nucleophilic substitution of hydrogen.
In the reported 2-chloro-substituted 1,4-naphthoquinone system, carbon addition at the hydrogen-bearing 3-position was substantially faster than addition at the chlorine-bearing 2-position.

Strongly basic tert-BuOK/THF conditions gave negative results and were associated with decomposition of the putative VNS products, whereas DBU enabled dimethyl chloromalonate and ethyl 2-chloroacetoacetate to react smoothly with substrate 1a to give the expected VNS products in good yields.
The reaction rate depended strongly on base strength and concentration; under low-base conditions the principal observed change was reduced VNS yield, with only negligible SNV product formation.

The authors proposed a two-step substitution pathway involving initial SNV formation of an intermediate, followed by cine substitution through carbon addition at the adjacent hydrogen-bearing position, proton transfer, chloride elimination, and base-induced beta-elimination.

Higher base concentration increased formation of the VNS product, whereas higher temperature favored formation of the H-adduct arising from addition at the hydrogen-bearing position; the authors related the temperature effect to accelerated dissociation and equilibration.
Under oxidative nucleophilic substitution conditions, the reported reaction gave only the product of oxidative substitution of hydrogen.

Alpha-halocarbanions reacted with the reported chloronitroarenes only through VNS, whereas analogous fluoronitrobenzenes gave SNAr and VNS products in a ratio dependent on base strength and concentration.
Formation of the observed product from the fluorinated quinone was rationalized by a speculative pathway beginning with SNV and followed by further reaction of the intermediate.
A chlorine substituent increased electrophilic activation and accelerated carbon addition at the hydrogen-bearing position, while fluorine showed a much weaker analogous effect.
Treatment of 1-phenylbuta-2,3-dien-1-one with 2 equivalents of TBAF·3H2O in water at 100 °C for 20 minutes afforded 3-fluoro-1-phenylbut-2-en-1-one as an E/Z mixture in 71% total yield.
The reported optimal fluorination conditions used 1 equivalent of allenic ketone, 3 equivalents of TBAF·3H2O, water, 100 °C, and 20 minutes, providing the β-fluoroenone in 81% yield.

Reactions run in refluxing dichloromethane, diethyl ether, acetonitrile, or THF gave complicated mixtures, whereas with 3 equivalents of KF, formation of β-fluoroenone 2a was not observed even over a prolonged reaction period.
Fluorination of the allenic ketones with TBAF·3H2O in water furnished β-fluoro-α,β-unsaturated ketones exclusively.

The authors propose that fluoride adds to the central allene carbon, followed by protonation to form the β-fluoro-α,β-unsaturated ketone; they also propose that a possible β,γ-unsaturated product would isomerize under the basic reflux conditions.
Aryl-substituted allenic ketones underwent fluorination, but electron-withdrawing substituents gave lower β-fluoroenone yields and were accompanied by 1,3-diketones attributed to allene hydration.

Substrates bearing a methyl group at the internal or terminal position of the allene moiety required longer reaction times; an unsaturated ester moiety was tolerated, and the tested simple alkyl-substituted substrate gave only a trace amount of the desired product.

The authors propose a reductive rearrangement pathway involving an initially formed β-hydroxyfluorovinyl alcohol, intramolecular nucleophilic addition, HF elimination to an oxetene intermediate, and ring opening to the enone.

An H2-18O experiment produced unlabeled 3a rather than 18O-labeled 3a; the authors state that this result may eliminate their alternative cation pathway because the proposed cation should have been trapped by labeled water.

The reductive defluorination rearrangement was demonstrated for eight β-fluoroenones using 3 equivalents of KBH4 in 1:1 water/methanol at room temperature for 4 hours, with isolated enone yields of 70-85%.
Fluoropyrazine was lithiated and quenched with multiple electrophiles to furnish substituted fluoropyrazines.
LTMP with a five-minute metallation time gave the best tested result for reaction of fluoropyrazine with acetaldehyde, affording the product in 86% yield.

The electrophile scope included aldehydes, benzophenone, ethyl formate, a sulfur electrophile, iodine, cyanogen bromide, and N,N-dimethyl amides, with reported yields ranging from 28% to 90% in Table 2.
Use of the sulfur electrophile also produced a 12% disubstituted side product, which the authors attributed to subsequent displacement of fluorine by phenylthiolate.
N,N-Dimethylacetamide and N,N-dimethylbenzamide produced fluorine-substitution side products bearing an N,N-dimethylamino group in 15% and 20% yield, respectively.
在THF、−78°C下使用4或5当量LTMP并配合所列亲电试剂时，化合物17及19–22的锂化尝试均未成功，且回收了起始物。
The authors proposed that bulky Ph2C(OH) or SiMe3 substituents could block approach of LTMP to the C5 position.

The authors proposed that lithium-alkoxide complexation creates steric hindrance that inhibits LTMP deprotonation, while also identifying alkoxide-triggered single-electron transfer as another possible explanation.
Cyclopropylboronic acid undergoes Suzuki-type C-C coupling with a range of aryl, heteroaryl, and vinyl bromides to give cyclopropyl adducts in good to excellent yields.

Condition screening used 1.2 equivalents of cyclopropylboronic acid; water significantly accelerated the coupling, and 5 mol% palladium acetate with 10 mol% tricyclohexylphosphine gave the best conversion among the reported screening conditions.

Under the optimized conditions, 1.3 equivalents of cyclopropylboronic acid coupled with 2-, 3-, 4-, and polysubstituted aryl bromides and tolerated ketone, ester, aldehyde, amine, nitrile, fluoro, and ether functionality; the phenol substrate showed no reaction.
A dibromide produced both a double Suzuki product in 60% yield and a singly coupled product arising from coupling at the ortho bromine.

Pyridines, quinolines, a furan, 2-bromonaphthoquinone, and a vinyl bromide gave the desired coupling products, whereas chlorobenzene, 1-chloro-4-nitrobenzene, and phenyl triflate did not react under the current conditions.

Under separately explored Buchwald aryl-chloride conditions, 1-chloro-4-nitrobenzene gave 20% product after 24 hours, while 4-chlorobenzaldehyde gave only trace product after 48 hours; the stated conditions used 10 mol% 2-(di-tert-butylphosphino)biphenyl, 5 mol% palladium acetate, three equivalents of potassium fluoride, THF, and 45 °C.

A representative aryl-bromide coupling procedure used aryl bromide, approximately 1.3 equivalents of cyclopropylboronic acid, potassium phosphate, 10 mol% tricyclohexylphosphine, 5 mol% palladium acetate, toluene-water, a nitrogen atmosphere, and heating at 100 °C for three hours.
Cyclopropylboronic acid showed no reaction with phenols or amines under the examined copper-catalyzed Chan-Evans coupling methods.

The isolated cyclopropylboronic acid typically contained 5-10% boric acid, which was not detrimental to the Suzuki reactions, and it showed no noticeable decomposition or activity loss over several months in a capped vial at room temperature.

The authors report a sequence from 2-fluoropyridines and carboxylic acids in which acylation with a Weinreb amide is followed by a one-pot, base-induced displacement and cyclization to give 2,3-carbon-disubstituted furo[2,3-b]pyridines.
For formation of ester-containing product 12a, sodium hydride and ethyl glycolate in THF at 60 °C for 12 hours afforded a 50% yield; intermediate 11a formed rapidly and cyclized more slowly.
DMAc accelerated the cyclization relative to THF: the reaction was complete in 1 hour at 60 °C and product 12a was isolated in 60% yield by water addition and filtration.
Carboxylic acids 13 and 14 were competitive by-products during ester cyclization and were attributed by the authors to hydrolysis of intermediate 11a and product 12a under the reaction conditions.
Replacing sodium hydride with Cs2CO3, sodium tert-butoxide, DIPEA, or DBU was unsuccessful: inorganic and amine bases produced little desired product, complex mixtures, or decomposition.
The reported 3-position scope included electron-rich and electron-deficient aryl groups and an alkyl group, although the alkyl-substituted product was obtained in lower yield.
Under the furo[2,3-b]pyridine conditions, the related thieno[2,3-b]pyridine 12e was prepared in a comparable yield after recrystallization from ethanol.

Alpha-hydroxy amides 20a-c reacted with ketone 8a under the established conditions to afford furo[2,3-b]pyridine amides 21a-c in good yields, and corresponding carboxylic-acid side products were not formed.

Direct application of the sodium hydride/DMAc conditions to alpha-hydroxy acetophenone and 8a gave no desired ketone 22; alternative bases gave no conversion, decomposition, or low-yield complex mixtures because alpha-hydroxy acetophenone was unstable under the strongly basic conditions.
Ketones 22 and 23 were instead obtained from amide 21b using PhLi, MeLi, or MeMgBr; the authors report excellent or similarly high yields and no observable impurities for the organolithium reactions.

The reported transformation is a tandem sequence comprising selective nucleophilic substitution of the 6-fluoride of a 2,6-difluoro-3-ketopyridine, hydrazine substitution of the remaining 2-fluoride, and pyrazole formation, furnishing 3,6-disubstituted 1H-pyrazolo[3,4-b]pyridines.

The general tandem procedure used 3 equivalents of the initial nucleophile in DMAc at 0-5 °C for 0.5-3 h, followed by 4 equivalents of hydrazine monohydrate at 0-5 °C and subsequent stirring at room temperature for 1-5 h.

Regioselectivity in the initial tert-butylamine SNAr step was strongly solvent-dependent: DMAc gave the 6-substituted and 2-substituted intermediates in a 4:1 ratio, while toluene reversed the preference and gave the 2-substituted intermediate selectively at a reported 16.7:1 ratio over the 6-substituted intermediate.

The authors tentatively attributed the solvent-dependent regioselectivity to hydrogen bonding: carbonyl-amine hydrogen bonding in nonpolar solvent was proposed to direct substitution toward C-2, whereas amine-solvent hydrogen bonding in polar solvent was proposed to favor substitution at the less hindered C-6 position.

Electronic and steric properties of substituents affected initial SNAr regioselectivity: a para electron-donating group reduced preference for the desired 6-substituted intermediate, electron-withdrawing substituents favored it, and ortho substitution increased its proportion.
The tert-butylamine series tolerated bromo, chloro, fluoro, methoxy, nitro, furanyl, and benzothiophenyl groups, and the one-pot products were reported in 51-84% overall yield.

Sulfur-, oxygen-, and nitrogen-centered nucleophiles were demonstrated: tert-butyl thiol and phenol gave highly regioselective 6-fluoride substitution and high overall yields, secondary amine and aniline reacted, and amino acids furnished products in moderate yields.
表3列出的六个不同亲核试剂实例中，报告的区域异构体比为1.2:1至20:1，一锅分离收率为43%至91%；这些数值在所列实例之间存在明显差异。
IF5-pyridine-HF 和氢醌可使所研究的一个内炔和一个端炔发生碘氟化，立体选择性地生成相应碘氟烯烃。
Terminal alkynes and both symmetrical and unsymmetrical internal alkynes furnished iodofluoroalkenes with reported stereo- and regioselectivity; electron-deficient alkynes were also successful.

Reductant choice strongly affected iodofluorination selectivity: KI produced no desired 2a and instead gave diiodoalkene 3a and iodoalkyne 4a, whereas catechol and hydroquinone suppressed those reported byproducts and gave 2a in 75% and 82% NMR yield, respectively.

The standard iodofluorination conditions were room temperature in dichloromethane with two equivalents each of IF5-pyridine-HF and hydroquinone; one electron-deficient example instead used 1,2-dichloroethane at 60 °C with four equivalents of each reagent.
Formation of p-quinone was confirmed in the reaction mixture during iodofluorination.

The authors propose that hydroquinone reduces IF5-pyridine-HF to an IF species that adds to the alkyne, but state that the actual active species responsible for selectivity cannot be identified because the IF species is unstable in solution.
2a 与有机硼烷进行 Suzuki-Miyaura 偶联，立体选择性地生成二取代氟烯烃 5 和 6。
Cross-coupling of trisubstituted iodofluoroalkene 2f with phenylboronic acid was sluggish; the electrophile decomposed and target 7 was not formed.
Replacing phenylboronic acid with phenyltriolborate overcame the failed coupling of 2f and afforded product 7 in 92% yield.
Additional Sonogashira and Suzuki-Miyaura reactions of iodofluoroalkenes furnished trisubstituted fluoroalkenes stereoselectively.

优化条件及通用操作使用β-氟代烯酮0.1 mmol、NaN3 0.3 mmol、MeCN 1.0 mL，在80 °C反应3 h；优化实验中模型产物3a的报告收率为96%。
Lowering the temperature from 80 °C to 60 °C reduced the 3 h yield to 66% and left about 30% starting material; extending the 60 °C reaction to 6 h gave 90% yield.
MeCN was the best tested solvent for the model reaction; MeCN/H2O gave 79%, while THF, ethyl acetate, DMF, toluene, acetone, and DCE were inferior under the reported comparison conditions.
芳环对位带OMe、Me或tBu的底物被报告可顺利反应并以优异收率得到产物；芳环带F、Cl、Br或NO2的底物给出51%至82%的报告收率。
Ortho-methyl and ortho-chloro aryl ketones gave products in 80% and 93% yields, and meta-substituted aryl examples gave 55–84% yields.

Naphthalene- and furan-containing substrates gave isoxazole products in good yields, while changing the stated R1 substituent to phenyl led to lower efficiency under the original conditions; THF improved one 1,3-diaryl example but another remained at 41% yield.

The authors propose that azide first substitutes the vinyl fluorine to form a vinyl azide, followed either by azirine formation and rearrangement or by direct 5-exo-trig cyclization through enolate oxygen attack; nitrogen release is proposed as the driving force.

DFT calculations place the path-A cyclization transition state 2.2 kcal/mol above path B and compute a 27.4 kcal/mol barrier and −36.5 kcal/mol reaction free energy for the path-B product-forming step.
Despite the computed preference for direct 5-exo-trig cyclization, the authors conclude that both proposed pathways may be accessible at the 80 °C reaction temperature.

Compounds 1–6 were synthesized by amino-defluorination of hexafluoro-1,4-naphthoquinone with n-butylamine, 2-methylthioethylamine, or 2,2′-dithiodiethylamine, establishing C–N bond formation with loss of fluorine on a polyfluorinated quinone electrophile.
Reaction of quinone 7 with a stated 1.5-fold excess of n-butylamine in 1,4-dioxane at room temperature gave predominantly the monosubstituted product 1, which was isolated in 63% yield.

Increasing the n-butylamine loading to a stated 3.6-fold excess produced a mixture of two disubstituted regioisomers and a trisubstituted product; compounds 2–4 were isolated in 12%, 30%, and 14% yield, respectively.
With 1.5 equivalents of 2-methylthioethylamine, quinone 7 formed practically a single amino-defluorination product after 2 h, isolated in 94% yield.
Reaction of two equivalents of quinone 7 with 2,2′-dithiodiethylamine at room temperature for 15 h gave compound 6 in 75% isolated yield.
The general synthesis used quinone 7 and the corresponding amine in dioxane at room temperature, with reaction times ranging from 2 to 48 h depending on the product.

Compounds 1–6 were characterized by NMR and elemental analysis or high-resolution mass spectrometry, and the structures of compounds 2 and 3 were additionally deduced by X-ray investigation.
The authors synthesized five polyfluorinated 1,4-naphthoquinone derivatives containing tert-butylamino, diethylamino, ethylamino, or phenylamino groups.
Compounds 1–4 were synthesized by aminodefluorination of hexafluoro-1,4-naphthoquinone 6, while compound 5 was synthesized by phenylaminodefluorination of 2-methylpentafluoro-1,4-naphthoquinone 7.
Hexafluoro-1,4-naphthoquinone 6 reacted readily with aliphatic amines at 17–27 °C to furnish compounds 1–3; compounds 2 and 3 were obtained after 2 h in practically quantitative isolated yields.

With tert-butylamine, the reaction plateaued at approximately 80% compound 1 and 20% starting material after 20 h; longer reaction times did not improve the major-product percentage and produced further-transformation products. Compound 1 was isolated in 62% yield.

Reaction of quinone 6 with aniline at room temperature for 15 h gave approximately 90% compound 4 and approximately 10% further-transformation products in the product mixture; compound 4 was isolated in 62% yield.
Quinone 7 reacted with aniline for 48 h to give approximately 80% compound 5 and approximately 20% further-transformation products in the product mixture; compound 5 was isolated in 26% yield.

Using quinone 6 and the corresponding free amine in dioxan, the reported isolated yields were 62% for tert-butylamino compound 1, 96% for diethylamino compound 2, and 62% for phenylamino compound 4.
Compounds 1–5 were characterized by 1H NMR, 19F NMR, elemental analysis, or high-resolution mass spectrometry.
The study synthesized farnesyltransferase inhibitors by transposing the D-ring of tipifarnib to the imidazole and modifying the 2-quinolone motif.
由酚33制得的三氟甲磺酸酯与1-萘硼酸进行Suzuki偶联，以46%收率生成醛34。

A second Suzuki coupling used 5-bromoindole and 1-naphthylboronic acid to prepare descyano compound 37a in 37% yield.

An attempted Barton–McCombie deoxygenation of alcohol 2a was unsuccessful.
Compound 4d was reported to have an FTase IC50 of 0.15 nM and a Ras-processing EC50 of 2.1 nM.

The authors prepared and evaluated a series of 5-methoxy- and 5-hydroxy-6-fluoro-1,8-naphthyridone-3-carboxylic acid derivatives.
In an early synthetic step, the authors report selective displacement of the 4-position fluoride of commercially available 3-chloro-2,4,5,6-tetrafluoropyridine with sodium methoxide.
Scheme 1 reports NaOMe in 1:1 MeOH–THF, initially at 0 °C and then warming to room temperature for 20 hours for the fluoride-to-methoxy substitution.
The authors selected azetidine, pyrrolidine, and aminopyrrolidine as three C7 amine variants and synthesized them from common core 9.
Displacement of the C7 fluorine by each selected amine proceeded smoothly in acetonitrile with Hünig's base and gave compounds 10a–c in high yield.
Scheme 2 specifies amine, DIPEA, acetonitrile, and 60 °C for the C7 substitution and reports 90–100% yield.
Conversion of the 5-methoxy compounds to the corresponding 5-hydroxy compounds used excess pyridine hydrochloride at approximately 140 °C for 10 minutes.
The reported 5-methoxy and 5-hydroxy products were structurally checked by proton NMR and mass spectrometry.

A fluorinated building block was prepared by adding an in situ generated trifluoromethyl anion to 2-fluoro-4-iodonicotinaldehyde, producing an aldol product; the text does not describe selective C-F cleavage in this step.
The authors converted an aryl iodide intermediate into aryl boronic acid pinacol ester 7.

For the adjacent-CF3 alcohol analogue 17, the authors observed improved rat liver S9 stability but greatly decreased PKC epsilon potency.
The authors conclude that proximal polar functionality mitigated direct O-glucuronidation more effectively than bulky lipophilic groups when potency permitted.

The authors report a Co-promoted coupling-aromatization-cyclization of polyfluorinated ketones with N- and S-nucleophiles involving quadruple C(sp3)-F bond cleavage and formation of regio-defined perfluoroalkylated naphtho[1,2-b]furan or benzofuran derivatives.

For the model reaction, 2-(perfluorobutyl)-3,4-dihydronaphthalen-1(2H)-one and 2-methylbenzimidazole gave product 3a in 74% NMR yield and 70% isolated yield using 10 mol% CoBr2, TBAB, Cs2CO3, DMSO, nitrogen, 70 °C, and 10 h.
CoBr2, TBAB, and base each improved the model reaction, but product still formed in 39% yield without CoBr2; omission of base reduced the result to trace product.

The model reaction gave 74% NMR yield and 71% isolated yield at room temperature; DMSO and Cs2CO3 were the best reported solvent and base in the supplied optimization tables, while MeNO2 and Li2CO3 gave no product.
作者展示的N亲核试剂包括苯并咪唑、咪唑、吲唑、吡唑、三唑、四唑、吲哚、吡咯、咔唑和嘌呤，所引段落报告的产物收率总体为36%至99%。
Aryl sulfur nucleophiles were demonstrated: 4-methylbenzenethiol and naphthalene-2-thiol afforded products 17 and 18 in 46% and 52% isolated yield, respectively.
The reported N-nucleophile limitation includes unsuccessful anilines, sulfonamide, and cyclic amine substrates.

In the absence of the N-nucleophile, base treatment produced compound 28 in 29% yield and byproduct 29 in less than 5%; independently subjected compound 28 afforded product 3a in 86% yield under coupling conditions.

The authors propose a mechanism involving Cs2CO3-assisted HF elimination, nucleophilic addition/fluoride elimination to form a coupled species, further desaturation and aromatization, and intramolecular O-nucleophilic vinylic substitution that cleaves a fourth C-F bond; they state that a 5-endo-trig pathway cannot be excluded.

The authors synthesized 6,13-difluoropentacene from 1,4-difluorobenzene through Friedel–Crafts chemistry, reduction, ortho-lithiation, reaction with phthalic anhydride, and removal of oxygen functionalities.

Initial attempts to prepare 6,13-difluoropentacene through a route beginning with 6,13-pentacenedione failed, leading the authors to investigate a route in which the central ring already carried both fluorine substituents.
The authors proposed that an intramolecular Friedel–Crafts-type acylation through acylium-cation intermediate 6 could form the indicated C5,5a bond.
The first Friedel–Crafts acylation used AlCl3 in boiling 1,4-difluorobenzene, and a second acylation in polyphosphoric acid at 140 °C afforded anthraquinone 11 in 53% yield over two steps.
Optimized ortho-lithiation used LDA at −78 °C for 15 minutes, followed by rapid addition of lithiated species 7 to phthalic anhydride in THF at −100 °C; carboxylic acid 12 was isolated in 82% yield.
PCl5 caused quantitative substitution of fluorine by chloride in the corresponding pentacenequinone; using polyphosphoric acid avoided this side reaction.
Diol 13 quantitatively decomposed to 6,13-pentacenequinone 15 in CD2Cl2 at room temperature within two hours.

The authors proposed that moisture could initiate degradation of diol 13 by intermolecular water attack to form fluorohydrin 14; they suggested an intramolecular pathway might operate without water, followed by HF elimination to pentacenequinone 15.
Aromatization of diol 13 with SnCl2 in 1,4-dioxane and aqueous HCl gave the target 6,13-difluoropentacene in 74% yield.
6,13-二氟并五苯在惰性气氛、−20 °C下储存一个月未见明显分解；但其CH2Cl2溶液在环境气氛和阳光下于3分钟内褪色，且1H NMR显示降解产物为6,13-并五苯醌15。
The complete route from 1,4-difluorobenzene gave 6,13-difluoropentacene in 7% yield over seven steps, with Friedel–Crafts acylations and ortho-directed lithiation identified as key steps.
Lewis acid catalysts convert methyl and ethyl fluoroalkyl alkyl ethers to fluorinated carbonyl compounds with loss of methyl fluoride or ethyl fluoride, respectively.
The reported product classes include acid fluorides, ketones, keto esters, vinyl ketones, acyl ketenes, ketenes, and acryloyl fluorides.

An early stoichiometric experiment heated 3-methoxyperfluoropropionyl fluoride with 1.5 equivalents of titanium tetrafluoride at 175 °C and afforded perfluoromalonyl fluoride and methyl fluoride in 77% yield.

The conversion was subsequently performed catalytically, exothermally, at atmospheric pressure and low temperature in high yield for multiple related compounds; antimony pentafluoride was identified as one of several effective metal-halide Lewis acid catalysts.
The author proposes that the mechanism may involve fluoride abstraction from a C-F bond to form an acid fluoride, a metal fluoride anion, and a methyl cation.

The author proposes that recombination of the metal fluoride anion and methyl cation could form methyl fluoride and regenerate the catalyst; an alternative concerted cyclic transition state is also suggested.

Because the reaction is exothermic, the author recommends controlling it by regulated addition of the ether into stirred neat catalyst; product may moderate the reaction and can sometimes be distilled from the mixture.

The reported structural scope links removal of methyl fluoride from -CF2OCH3 groups to acid fluoride formation, -CF(OCH3)- groups to ketone formation, and specified unsaturated fluoroethers to ketenes and/or acryloyl fluorides.

The reactions summarized in Table I used catalyst in a dried stirred still pot, portionwise substrate addition, and product distillation; most reactions were highly exothermic, some began below room temperature, and heat was applied when necessary.
Ethyl ethers are within the demonstrated scope: catalytic removal of ethyl fluoride was reported for two examples.

A TiF4-catalyzed example converted an isomeric methyl-ether mixture to an acryloyl fluoride in 86.5% isolated mass yield with methyl fluoride evolution, followed by conversion of that product to an acylketene in 90.8% yield.

The tetrafluoro-p-benzoquinone cyclopentadiene bisadduct undergoes facile addition of oxygen nucleophiles at a carbonyl group, followed by reaction of the carbonyl adduct with the double bond of the endo-bicycloheptene moiety.
Bisadduct 3 is highly susceptible to nucleophilic attack, and hydroxide and methoxide ions react readily with its carbonyl groups.
Elemental-composition data exclude assignment of the hydroxide and methoxide adducts as Favorskii rearrangement products.
NMR data indicate participation of the endo-bicycloheptene double bond and formation of a new carbon-oxygen bond at that site.

The authors propose initial oxygen-nucleophile attack on an electron-deficient carbonyl to form tetrahedral intermediate 8, followed by a proximity-favored process involving the endo-bicycloheptene double bond.
底物3与氢氧化钠在3:1二氧六环/水中于102 °C回流1小时，得到粗产物6，收率83%。
底物3与氢氧化钠在甲醇中于室温24小时内完全反应；重结晶前得到95%收率的无色晶体，重结晶后所得产物被标为7。
双加合物5在类似氢氧化物条件下未观察到相应的三环醚，而发生了羰基α位碳原子的差向异构化。
The fluorinated monoadduct 2b is extremely susceptible to nucleophilic attack, and exposure to hot methanol during recrystallization produced methoxy analogue 4 in good yield.

The paper describes the synthesis and chemistry of a perfluoroacylketene 12 and a related perfluorovinyl ketone 5, both prepared from a hexafluoropropene dimer and characterized as thermally stable but highly reactive.
Vinyl ketone 5 undergoes nucleophilic attack at its terminal unsaturated carbon and participates as a diene in additions to several classes of unsaturation.
The authors propose that electron-withdrawing fluorine atoms activate compounds 5 and 12 toward electron-rich dienophiles and other nucleophiles.
Vinyl ketone 5 was produced by vapor-phase dehydrofluorination of ketone 4 over sodium fluoride at 450 °C, with hydrogen fluoride eliminated; the discussion reports a 76% yield.

Both acylketene 12 and vinyl ketone 5 are storage-stable but readily hydrolyze with decarboxylation to ketone 13; hydrolysis of vinyl ketone 5 additionally releases two equivalents of HF according to the reported equation.
With cesium fluoride in tetraglyme and no heating, vinyl ketone 5 reacted exothermally and only HF adduct 4 was isolated, whereas acylketene 12 dimerized to 15.
Vinyl ketone 5 and acylketene 12 underwent very exothermic Diels-Alder additions to alkyl vinyl ethers and gave stable liquid adducts.
The reported vinyl-ketone reactions were stereospecific in hexane and glyme, whereas the reported acylketene reactions in hexane or chloroform were nonstereospecific.

The authors interpret stereospecific vinyl-ketone additions as indicating a concerted mechanism and suggest that at least part of the nonstereospecific acylketene reaction may proceed through a zwitterionic intermediate.

Reactions of vinyl ketone 5 with acetylenes were not clean, with the authors associating this limitation with labile fluorine atoms; phenylacetylene in the presence of sodium fluoride furnished multiple isolated or proposed products.
Vinyl ketone 5 and acylketene 12 reacted exothermally with acetaldehyde, benzaldehyde, and acetone through addition to the carbonyl group.
The authors prepared vinyl ketone 13 and acylketene 14 containing a perfluoroisopropyl sulfide group and investigated reactions of acylketene 14.
9与三氧化硫反应生成乙烯基酮13，后者在后处理过程中部分水解为酰基烯酮14。引文另提到10、11或12与三氧化硫反应会形成某一产物，但所给文字未明确指认该产物。
Preparation of acylketene 14 from ether ester 10 with sulfur trioxide gave 51 g (94%) of 14 while keeping the exothermic reaction below 65 °C.

14与异丁烯反应生成环状加合物20并伴有少量开链加合物21；与苯乙烯反应生成环状加合物22，而酸性条件下生成开链加合物23。14与乙酸乙烯酯发生伴随乙酸脱除的Diels–Alder加成生成24，并分别与苯乙炔和丁基乙炔反应生成25和26。

Carbonyl-partner scope showed stability and isolation limitations: propionaldehyde and benzaldehyde adducts were isolated, the propionaldehyde adduct reverted during attempted distillation, and no acetone adduct was isolated.
Under fluoride-ion-catalysis conditions that reacted with the comparison acylketene 15, acylketene 14 remained unchanged.

The authors assigned different nucleophilic sites for reactions of the two acylketenes with DMF: oxygen attack on 15 with loss of carbon dioxide versus nitrogen attack on 14 with loss of carbon monoxide.

Weak amide bases promoted self-condensation of acylketene 14 with loss of carbon dioxide to give pyrone 43, whose structure was confirmed by X-ray analysis; the corresponding reaction was not observed for acylketene 15.
The authors postulated that self-condensation proceeds through equilibrium formation of unsaturated lactone 41, carbon-dioxide loss to acetylene 42, and addition of 42 to the acylketene.
An alpha-trifluoromethyl ketone reacted with allyl ethyl carbonate under palladium catalysis at room temperature to form the allylated quaternary-carbon product in excellent yield.
The representative procedure used 3a, allyl ethyl carbonate, 4 mol% Pd(PPh3)4, THF, an argon atmosphere, room temperature, and 1.5 hours, affording isolated product 5a in 96% yield.
Palladium was required under the tested conditions: no product was obtained without a palladium catalyst or with PPh3 alone.

Pd(OAc)2 with PPh3 also furnished the product in good yield, whereas the supplied table reports no reaction for PdCl2, PdCl2/PPh3, Pd(OAc)2 alone, or PPh3 alone under their respective tested conditions.

The alpha-trifluoromethyl ketone scope included substrates bearing varied phenyl substituents, an aryl group on the carbonyl side, and fully aliphatic substrates, with reported moderate-to-excellent yields.
Fluoroalkyl ketones 3g and 3h with longer fluoroalkyl chains failed to give the desired allylation products and instead furnished dehydrofluorinated compounds in moderate yields.
Attempted reaction of compounds 3 with aldehydes under basic conditions did not create the desired quaternary carbon center because dehydrofluorination occurred.
Allyl-partner identity and leaving group imposed scope boundaries: the authors concluded that only allyl carbonates were usable, while one tested allyl compound was recovered and another decomposed.
For smoothly reacting substituted allyl partners, substitution occurred at the less hindered allylic position; both tested geometric isomers 4h and 4i gave the same E product 5i.

The authors proposed a catalytic sequence involving oxidative addition of palladium into the allyl carbonate, decarboxylation to a pi-allyl alkoxy palladium complex, deprotonation of ketone 3, formation of intermediate 9, and reductive elimination to product 5 with regeneration of Pd(0).
The authors hypothesized that the decreased yield associated with allyl phenyl carbonate 4b might result from the weaker basicity of the derived phenoxide and/or steric hindrance.
Terminal alkynes undergo difunctionalization with AgF and NBS as the fluorine and bromine sources.
作者报告的最佳条件为2.5当量AgF、乙腈、80 °C和10小时。
在所述条件下，溴氟化产物以95%收率形成，且仅得到cis产物，并未检测到苯乙炔基溴化物2a'。
The reaction requires a stoichiometric amount of AgF rather than merely a catalytic quantity.
CsF/AgNO3体系仅产生痕量目标溴氟化产物，并以苯乙炔基溴化物2a'为主要副产物（86%）；pyridinium/Pd(OAc)2、CuF2/AgBF4和NiF2/AgNO3体系对该溴氟化无效。作者还报告若干常见氟源给出与前文相似的结果，但所给引文不足以确定这些结果的具体性质。
The terminal-alkyne scope included aryl alkynes bearing electron-donating or electron-withdrawing substituents and tolerated Cl, Br, F, CN, CF3, NO2, and OMe groups.
Ethynyltrimethylsilane failed to furnish a bromofluoroalkene and instead afforded fluorotrimethylsilane.
作者将反应扩展到取代芳基炔基酮等电子缺陷化合物；所考察的苯基炔基酮形成相应氟化产物，并报告了良好收率或高Z/E选择性。
A bromofluoroalkene reacted with phenylboronic acid to give a fluoroalkene bearing a new aryl substituent in 91% yield.
Direct fluorination experiments showed that both bromoalkynes and chloroalkynes gave fluorination products exclusively in good yields.

The authors propose formation of a bromoalkyne followed by a silver pi-complex, trans-addition of AgF to form a vinyl-silver intermediate, and protonation to furnish the Z bromofluoroalkene; they attribute regio- and stereoselectivity to backside fluoride attack.
Terminal alkynes undergo difunctionalization using AgF and NBS as halogen sources.

The optimized bromofluorination used 2.5 equivalents of AgF in acetonitrile at 80 °C for 10 h and gave the product in 95% yield exclusively as the cis isomer; the authors characterize AgF as a stoichiometric mediator.
Common fluoride sources and several Ag- or Pd-containing systems were ineffective or produced only traces, while the CsF/AgNO3 system mainly formed phenylethynyl bromide.

The bromofluorination scope included aromatic terminal alkynes bearing electron-donating or electron-withdrawing groups and tolerated Cl, Br, F, CN, CF3, NO2, and OMe substituents; aliphatic alkynes were also suitable.
Ethynyltrimethylsilane did not furnish the target bromofluoroalkene and instead afforded fluorotrimethylsilane.

Phenyl alkynyl ketones afforded fluorination products in good yields and with high Z/E selectivities, and 3-phenyl-1-(thiophen-2-yl)prop-2-yn-1-one afforded a hydrofluorination product in good yield under the applied conditions.
Pd/Cu-catalyzed coupling of bromofluoroalkenes with terminal alkynes gave 1-fluoro-1,3-enyne products in good yields.
One bromofluoroalkene, 2f, reacted with phenylboronic acid to give a fluorinated alkene product in 91% yield.
Direct fluorination experiments showed that both bromoalkynes and chloroalkynes gave fluorination products exclusively and in good yields.
The authors interpret their control experiments as evidence consistent with, but not definitive proof of, a haloalkyne intermediate.

The authors propose Ag-catalyzed formation of a bromoalkyne, silver coordination, trans-addition of AgF to form a vinyl-silver intermediate, and protonation to furnish the Z bromofluoroalkene; they state that an alternative fluoride-addition pathway cannot be excluded.

The reported transformation is a one-pot dehydrochlorination followed by trans-hydrofluorination of beta-chloro-alpha,beta-unsaturated aldehydes or ketones, producing trisubstituted beta-monofluoroalkenes.
For the model beta-chloroenal, the reported optimum was KHF2 (2.5 equivalents) in DMSO at 130 degrees C, giving product 3a in 62% yield and a 98:2 Z/E ratio.

Aromatic beta-chloroenals bearing electron-withdrawing or electron-donating substituents furnished beta-fluoroenals in low-to-moderate yields with 97:3 to 99:1 Z/E ratios; electron-withdrawing para substituents accelerated the reaction, whereas para-methyl and para-methoxy substituents retarded it.

The enal scope showed reduced performance for a thienyl substrate and an alkenyl substituent: the thienyl substrate gave a lower yield and slightly lower Z/E ratio, while replacing the beta-aryl group with an alkenyl group gave low yield and decreased stereoselectivity.

Under the optimized enone conditions, structurally varied beta-chloroenones, including heteroaromatic vinyl ketone 4f and alkyl vinyl ketone 4h, were converted with (n-Bu)4N+H2F3- and AgF to beta-fluoroenones 6a–6m in moderate yields and 98:2 to greater than 99:1 Z/E ratios.

Silver salts were required for hydrofluorination of the model alkynone under the tested catalytic conditions: no fluorination occurred without silver salts, Pd(OAc)2 gave no observed product, and CuI gave only alkynone 5a.

The control experiments were consistent with an alkynyl-carbonyl intermediate: beta-chloroenals 7a and 7b lacking an alpha hydrogen did not undergo dehydrochlorination, a tested substrate lacking beta chlorine gave no desired 3a, and independently supplied alkynal 2a and alkynone 5a underwent trans-hydrofluorination.

The authors propose that enals react through base-promoted alkynal formation, nucleophilic HF2- attack, an alkenyl anion, and protonation, while enones react through an alkynyl ketone-silver pi complex, backside fluoride attack to a vinyl-silver intermediate, and protonolysis.
Under the optimized fluorination conditions, beta-chlorovinyl ketone 4n unexpectedly underwent furan formation.
The paper reports that Suzuki coupling of compound 10 with phenylboronic acid gave functionalized (E)-fluorostilbene 12 in 75% yield.
The authors report rhodium-catalyzed allylic cyanation of 3-fluoroallylic trifluoroacetates with TMSCN and a bulky phosphite ligand to form 3-fluoroallylic nitriles with high Z/E selectivity.
Under the optimized 5 mol% catalyst conditions, Rh(PPh3)3Cl and phosphite ligand 10 in THF at 70 °C for 4 h afforded model nitrile 9 in 72% yield with an 11:1 Z/E ratio.
在Pd催化的8a→9模型反应中，CuCN、NaCN或ZnCN作为氰源时起始物不发生转化；改用TMSCN并使用Pd(PtBu3)2时，仅得到痕量目标产物。
Changing the leaving group from acetate to trifluoroacetate improved the palladium-catalyzed model yield from 52% to 61%, although the palladium system had low Z/E selectivity.

The reaction tolerated a variety of functional groups and diprotected amines, but steric hindrance alpha to the R1 residue appeared to suppress reaction, whereas alpha steric hindrance at R2 had no significant reactivity effect.
Aromatic substituents were a limitation: benzylic trifluoroacetates decomposed readily at higher temperature, required catalyst loading above 5%, and furnished cyanation products in yields below 50%.

Fluorinated substrates gave exclusively the distal regioisomer in the reported scope, whereas the corresponding nonfluorinated substrate produced a 2:1 distal/proximal mixture, supporting a decisive fluorine substituent effect on regioselectivity.
A stereochemical correlation experiment established inversion of the stereocenter during cyanation of substrate 12j; another substrate, 12a, underwent stereoerosion from 97% ee to 86% ee.
The authors propose that fluorine coordination to rhodium, in addition to an electronic effect, may shift the equilibrium among proposed intermediates 22-24 and favor distal product formation.

The authors suggest that the fluorine-controlled regioselectivity observed with cyanide could be applicable to other nucleophiles, but no such nucleophile classes are demonstrated in the supplied text.
The preparative procedure used 5 mol% rhodium catalyst, 20 mol% phosphite 10, five equivalents of TMSCN, THF, and 70 °C for 4 h, affording rac-13a in 72% yield and 11:1 Z/E ratio.

The paper demonstrates transition-metal-free successive C(sp3)-F functionalization of polyfluoroalkylated ketones with sulfur and oxygen nucleophiles, producing partially fluorinated polycyclic furan and chromene derivatives through a coupling, aromatization, and cyclization cascade.
1a与1,2-二苯基二硫烷在TBAB（1.0当量）、Cs2CO3（2.5当量）和氯仿中于70 °C反应12小时，得到3a，NMR收率73%、分离收率60%。
对该具体转化，作者的对照实验表明TBAB和Cs2CO3是必要的；以K2CO3、NaOH、tBuOK或DABCO替代Cs2CO3时未生成3a，且DCE、甲苯、DMSO和MeCN不如CHCl3有效。

Aryl disulfides bearing bromo, chloro, fluoro, or methyl substituents and one heteroaryl disulfide were compatible, whereas dipropyl disulfide gave an unexpected alkene product in 17% yield and a benzyl-substituted disulfide substrate was unsuitable.
所给引文报告了富电子和缺电子芳基硫酚的反应；邻位含Br、F或OMe的实例5c、5f和5i收率为84–92%，且5c可在1 mmol规模以84%收率制备。

Variation of the polyfluoroalkylated ketone included substituted perfluorobutyl tetralones, a heteroaromatic analogue, and perfluoroalkyl chains ranging from three to ten carbons; the authors report highly regioselective C-F cleavage in all of these cases.

Oxygen-nucleophile reactions were demonstrated but showed outcome sensitivity: reagent 8 gave ether 9 and uncyclized byproduct 10 in 25% and 38% yields, while 4-bromophenol gave difunctionalized chromene 12 in 19% yield under modified conditions.
在作者进行的对照实验中，环己酮类似物17未检出预期产物，七元环底物19的尝试也未成功。作者据此认为，在该反应体系中羰基邻位的苯环或共轭C=C键是必要的，并提出自动芳构化可能对连续C-F键断裂很重要。

Under basic conditions, substrate 1a eliminated HF to form defluorinated alkene intermediate 22 as a 1:1 E/Z mixture; unsaturated compound 23 was subsequently converted to product 5c in 52% yield under the standard conditions.

Additive effects were substrate- or context-dependent: absence of TBAB inhibited formation of 5c and gave compound 23 in 27% yield, but TBAI produced 5c in 75% yield, whereas LiBr and CoBr2 did not promote the desired cyclization.
作者提出如下机理假说：Cs2CO3先促进多氟烷基酮脱HF形成不饱和酮，随后发生S/O亲核试剂的1,4-加成、进一步C-F键断裂和β,γ-去饱和；这些步骤属于作者提出的机理，而非由所给实验完整确立的机理。
β,β-Difluoro peroxides undergo base-promoted cyclocondensation with 5-amino-1H-pyrazoles to furnish 5,7-disubstituted pyrazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidines.
The standard procedure uses peroxide 1 (0.2 mmol), 5-amino-1H-pyrazole 2a (0.4 mmol), DABCO (0.6 mmol), and 1,4-dioxane (2.0 mL) at 60 °C for 6 h.

Among the quoted solvent-screen entries, 1,4-dioxane with DABCO at 60 °C gave the best reported result, with table values of 77% for 3a, 73% in parentheses, and 8% for 3a'; the authors state that regioselectivity depends on the solvent.
DABCO outperformed the other reported bases: TMEDA gave 54% 3a, while pyridine, triethylamine, DBU, and K2CO3 gave poor results, including no detected 3a with K2CO3.
Lowering the reaction temperature from 60 °C to 25 °C reduced the 3a yield to 54%, whereas 80 °C gave 74%, close to the 60 °C result.

Aryl-substituted β-perfluoro peroxides bearing electron-donating or electron-withdrawing groups at ortho, meta, or para positions were tolerated, and naphthalene- and furan-containing substrates gave products in 67% and 74% yield, respectively.
An aliphatic-substituted β-perfluoro peroxide bearing C6H13 gave the desired product 3n in only 12% yield even at 120 °C.
The authors attribute the low efficiency of the C6H13-substituted peroxide to difficult formation of the corresponding alkyl ketone during the initial Kornblum-DeLaMare rearrangement.
Peroxide-derived substituent classes installed at the 5-position included esters, ketones, amides, and trifluoromethyl groups under the optimized conditions.
Control experiments formed β-fluoro enone 5 from the peroxide in the absence of aminopyrazole 2a, and isolated 5 subsequently furnished 3a in 91% yield when treated with 2a.
4,4,4-Trifluoro-1-phenylbut-2-en-1-one 6 did not furnish expected product 4j; the authors interpret this result as showing that a β-fluorine leaving group is crucial.

The authors propose that DABCO promotes peroxide rearrangement to a ketone, HF elimination forms a β-fluoro enone, and aminopyrazole then reacts by nucleophilic addition-elimination followed by cyclization and rearomatization; an alternative condensation pathway is also proposed for the minor regioisomer.
作者报道了蓝光促进的炔烃氧化二氟烷基化；通过稍微调整反应条件，可以选择性合成β-氟代烯酮或α-二氟烷基酮。
表2所列标准条件A使用1（0.2 mmol）、2（0.4 mmol）、fac-Ir(ppy)3（2 mol%）、Li2CO3（1.5 equiv）、bpy（20 mol%）、H2O（0.12 mL）和MeCN（2 mL）进行β-氟代烯酮合成。
Omission of carbonate redirected the model reaction from β-fluoroenone 3a to α-difluoroalkyl ketone 4a; adding 20 mol% bpy gave 4a in 74% isolated yield.
在表1第16项标为“Without PC or hν”的测试条件下，β-氟代烯酮3a的报告产率为0；作者据此认为光敏剂和蓝光对该炔烃二氟烷基化是必要的。
一级和二级烷基取代炔烃可生成产物3a–3g，收率为62–78%，E/Z=99/1；底物1a在6 mmol规模反应中以65%分离收率得到3a。

Scope limitations included poor yield for a cyano-substituted alkyne, no product from an unprotected terminal alkyne, only 20% yield and reduced E-selectivity for a trimethylsilyl-protected terminal alkyne, and 23% yield with poor stereoselectivity from diphenylacetylene.
Methanol was tested as an oxygen nucleophile and generated product 7 in 47% yield, demonstrating capture by an oxygen nucleophile other than water under this reaction manifold.

A TEMPO trapping experiment produced TEMPO-CF2CO2Et in 77% isolated yield with only trace desired product, and a 1,1-diphenylethene trapping experiment generated adduct 9; these experiments support involvement of a CF2CO2Et radical.

The authors propose photoinduced single-electron formation of a CF2CO2Et radical, radical addition to the alkyne, oxidation of the resulting vinyl radical to a vinyl carbocation, capture by water or alcohol to form the α-difluoroalkyl ketone, and base-promoted E2 elimination to form the (E)-β-fluoroenone.
使用过量水合肼处理时，作者以77%收率得到其所称的亲核脱氟产物15。
The reported transformation is a one-pot Fischer-type indole synthesis based on condensation of quinone monoketals with aliphatic hydrazines.
Treatment of quinone monoketal 1a with methylhydrazine or N,N-dimethylhydrazine gave only polar intractable products, and the desired nonpolar alkylaryldiazene was not detected.
Addition of acetic acid enabled isolation of methyldiazene 5a in 23% yield as a 40:1 E/Z mixture, while the remaining material was an unidentified mixture of polar side products.
The authors suggest that general acid catalysis facilitates dehydration of a carbinolhydrazine intermediate and that steric hindrance in bulkier hydrazines may disfavor competing 1,4-addition.

The optimized one-pot process used quinone monoketal 1a and cyclohexylhydrazine hydrochloride 2c heated in chloroform with two equivalents of pyridine in a sealed vial, affording tetrahydrocarbazole 7ac in 68% yield.

The authors propose that a weak base promotes diazene formation and that its conjugate acid mediates diazene-to-hydrazone isomerization, ene-hydrazine formation, and the Fischer-type rearrangement to indole.
Table 2 reports isolated indole-product yields of 41% to 95% for the listed quinone-derived substrates 1a–1p, including explicitly labeled I-, Br-, Cl-, and F-substituted examples.

The reported hydrazine scope included N-n-alkylhydrazines, N-sec-alkylhydrazines, cyclopentylhydrazine, and cycloheptylhydrazine; the authors described the corresponding yields as moderate to good or similar to that of 7ac.
For unsymmetrical hydrazine 2h, the authors observed a regioselective product but only proposed that weak medium acidity accounts for the selectivity.
The authors describe the overall method as a two-step synthesis from phenols and aliphatic hydrazines that avoids arylhydrazines, diazonium intermediates, and transition metals.
Bimetallic reagents of general formula R'2Zn·2LiOR converted a wide range of aryl and heteroaryl iodides or bromides into diaryl- and diheteroarylzinc species in toluene within 10 minutes to 5 hours.
The exchange chemistry tolerated sensitive triazine, ketone, aldehyde, and nitro functional groups, and the resulting organozinc species were functionalized by quenching with electrophiles.
对于目标二芳基锌物种 5a，含一个氮配位位点的烷氧基试剂 1b 给出 95% GC 收率；含第二个氮配位位点的 1c 加快交换，并在 1 min 后给出 99% GC 收率。
A representative organozinc reagent underwent palladium-catalyzed Negishi coupling with ethyl 4-iodobenzoate using Pd(OAc)2 (3 mol%) and SPhos (6 mol%), affording a biaryl in 76% yield.
Electron-poor aryl iodides bearing ester or nitrile groups underwent exchange, and subsequent reactions with various electrophiles furnished products in reported yields of 59–98%.
The method also supported Br/Zn exchange: 4-bromobenzonitrile reacted with 1c in toluene at 25 °C for 5 hours, and iodine quenching afforded 4-iodobenzonitrile in 77% yield.
2,4-Dinitroiodobenzene 经 1c 处理时，观察到起始物分解。
NMR monitoring showed that Et2Zn alone was inert toward exchange with 2-iodoanisole; adding one equivalent of LiOR gave 23% conversion after 10 minutes, whereas two equivalents gave 95% conversion.

The authors assign the major solution species as the contact-ion-pair lithium zincate [sBu2Zn(OR)2Li2] and tentatively assign a minor ethyl-containing complex; these structural assignments are described as consistent with the NMR data rather than conclusively established.

The authors propose that nitrogen-donor alkoxide coordination to lithium may explain the alkoxide effect because alkoxides lacking nitrogen donors may form less-reactive, higher oligomeric lithium zincates.

X-ray crystallography of [Me2Zn·LiOR] provided structural evidence for a lithium diorganoalkoxyzincate containing zinc bound to two methyl groups and an alkoxide ligand, with lithium atoms bridged through oxygen and coordinated by nitrogen atoms in the alkoxide chain.
该论文报告了酰胺与2′-(拟)卤代苯乙酮的镍催化C–N交叉偶联方法，并称该方法可生成4-喹诺酮。
优化体系采用(L4)Ni(4-CN-Ph)Cl（L4=PAd2-DalPhos）预催化剂以及DBU/NaTFA有机碱/卤离子清除体系。

Representative scope reactions used amide at 1.1 equivalents, DBU and NaTFA at 2.0 equivalents each, toluene, and 18 hours; the extracted text does not give a single universal nickel loading or temperature for every scope entry.
Successful nitrogen-nucleophile scope included electron-rich, electron-poor, and hindered benzamides, as well as formamide and trifluoroacetamide.

Cyclopropylamide, heteroaryl-containing substrates, 2-oxazolidinone, and electrophiles bearing trifluoromethyl, fluoro, methyl, or methoxy substituents were compatible; no cyclopropyl ring opening was observed.

Several common ligands performed poorly in screening: negligible conversion was obtained with IPr, DPE-Phos, or DPPF, and the previously used CyPAd-DalPhos system was inferior to PAd2-DalPhos under the tested conditions.
DBU and NaTFA were both important for efficient turnover, while DBU hydrochloride inhibited catalysis.
COD inhibited the reaction, with increasing added COD causing diminished formation of A2.
Room-temperature coupling was demonstrated: at 25 °C with 3 mol% (L4)Ni(4-CN-Ph)Cl, formation of A1 and A2 each exceeded 80% conversion; reducing nickel loading to 1 mol% gave inferior results.
作者提出其观察结果支持Ni(0)/Ni(II)催化循环，并推测加热时生成未观察到的(L4)Ni(2-Ac-Ph)(amido)中间体，随后可能经C–N还原消除形成产物及相应镍配合物。

The paper reports cationic Rh(I)/tetrafluoroborate-catalyzed cleavage of an acyl fluoride C-F bond and intramolecular addition across a tethered alkene, furnishing tertiary alkyl fluoride derivatives by 1,2-carbofluorination.
Acyl fluoride 1a gave insertion product 2a in 70% isolated yield under the reported standard conditions: 10 mol% [Rh(cod)2]BF4, 10 mol% dppbz, DCE, 90 °C, sealed vial.

Pd(0) and Ni(0) species failed to promote the desired insertion; no product formed without rhodium, neutral [RhCl(cod)]2 was inactive, and lowering the temperature to 70 °C gave no reaction. Omitting dppbz reduced rather than eliminated product formation.
在所报道体系中，作者考察的单取代烯烃和内烯烃未参与碳氟化；含短一个碳系链的底物 1m 得到酚衍生物 2m'，而非拟合成的六元环碳氟化产物 2m。

Tethered alkynes also underwent carbofluorination, but with six-membered 6-exo selectivity; a substrate bearing both an alkyne and alkene gave simple alkyne acylfluorination rather than the attempted tandem double cyclization.
Changing the rhodium counterion from BF4- to SbF6- prevented formation of 2a and instead gave alkene 2a' in 40% yield; adding one equivalent of nBu4NBF4 restored formation of 2a in 46% yield.

External-nucleophile trapping experiments produced Friedel-Crafts acylation products with anisole under either BF4- or SbF6-based cationic rhodium catalysis and allylated products with allylsilane under SbF6 conditions.

Replacing the Rh/BF4/dppbz system with BF3·OEt2 did not furnish the carbofluorination product and instead produced a complicated mixture.

The authors developed an Au(I)-catalyzed tandem reaction that transfers an equivalent of HF from a pentafluoropyridine/4-methoxyphenol pair to diphenylacetylene. Substituted phenols and anilines functioned as O- and N-centered nucleophiles in pentafluoropyridine functionalization, although anilines generally gave lower relative yields of the fluoroalkene coproduct than phenols.
Fluoroarene reactivity declined for less electron-deficient substrates, and the reported fluoroarene scope was limited to systems susceptible to SNAr.

Symmetric and asymmetric internal alkynes, including alkyl and aryl examples and substrates bearing electron-donating or electron-withdrawing groups or a free alcohol, underwent HF-transfer hydrofluorination.

Under the reported scope-expansion conditions, the tested terminal alkynes (hex-1-yne and ethynylbenzene) and tested silylated alkynes (trimethyl(phenylethynyl)silane and 1,2-bis(trimethylsilyl)ethyne) did not give hydrofluorination products.

For the reported kinetic experiment, the empirical rate was first order in HX, fluoroarene, and catalyst; the alkyne order was not determined because the reaction had to be run with more than two equivalents of alkyne.

Changing the nucleophile from 4-methoxyphenol to 4-methoxyaniline changed the observed kinetics: formation of the fluoroalkene was suggested to be zeroth order in fluoroarene and first order in HX, and the measured isotope effect increased from 1.1 ± 0.1 for the phenol to 2.8 ± 0.3 for the aniline.

For pentafluoropyridine, 4-methoxyphenol, and diphenylacetylene, products 1a and 2a formed concurrently and no HF buildup was observed. With 4-methoxyaniline, formation of 1h occurred independently of formation of 2a, and the authors identified HF as a reaction intermediate from a broad, concentration-dependent 19F NMR resonance at δ 150.5-152.5 ppm.

The authors propose a nucleophile-dependent catalytic network in which cSNAr is expected to be slow and turnover-limiting for phenol-based nucleophiles, whereas the hydrofluorination sequence is slow and likely turnover-limiting for aniline-based nucleophiles. They further suggest that direct protodeauration with HX may be a minor pathway and that reaction of [Au(IPr)F] with HX could provide a bypass that generates HF.
Adding 1.2 equivalents of 4-methoxyphenol to the aniline reaction preserved exclusive formation of the aniline SNAr product while increasing the fluoroalkene yield from 50 ± 2% to 72 ± 3%.
The paper reports an Au(I/III)-catalyzed oxidative C-C cross-coupling between electron-rich heteroarenes or carbocyclic arenes and electron-poor arenes through double C-H activation.

Under the initial stoichiometric conditions, the expected stoichiometric coupling product formed in 9% yield out of a possible 10%, but the catalytic product was not detected, indicating failure of electron-poor-arene C-H activation and catalytic turnover.
Stoichiometric bases, with or without Ag(I) salts, completely inhibited the cross-coupling, whereas omission of stoichiometric base and use of substoichiometric AgOPiv enabled catalytic turnover.
The optimized example used PPh3AuCl, PBX, and AgOPiv at 110 °C; N-TIPS-indole gave 77% NMR yield and 73% isolated yield.
Ag salt was necessary even with PPh3AuOPiv as catalyst, while phosphine-free Au sources remained catalytically active but gave lower yields than PPh3AuCl.

The coupling tolerated thioether, benzylic aldehyde, benzylic alcohol, nitrile, nitro, protected amine, ester, ketone, fluorinated pyridine, and carbon-halogen functionality, but free amines were incompatible.

Electron-poor-arene reactivity declined as electron deficiency decreased; two fluorines ortho to the activated position were important, and fluorobenzene and 1,4-difluorobenzene produced only trace coupling products.

Reported electron-rich partners included TIPS-protected pyrrole, 2,3-dimethylfuran, 2-methylthiophene, benzothiophene, and several electron-rich carbocyclic arenes; benzothiophene showed excellent reactivity but poor regioselectivity.

Near-stoichiometric substrate ratios retained cross-selectivity: 1.5 equivalents of pentafluorobenzene gave 70% yield, and 1.5 equivalents of tetrafluoropyridine gave 63% yield, without observed homocoupling in the former experiment.

The authors state that the exact mechanism is unclear; they interpret electron-rich-arene scope and regioselectivity as consistent with Au(III) C-H activation and suggest possible Ag involvement in electron-poor-arene C-H activation.

Cross-coupling at the aryl bromide sites proceeded without concomitant olefination; the para- and meta-substituted substrates coupled in high yield, while the ortho-substituted substrate required ligand optimization and QPhos proved optimal.
Amination of the aryl bromides with aniline or morpholine proceeded smoothly and furnished the corresponding products in high yield.
The authors identify defluorinative amination under basic conditions as a known reactivity of unmasked trifluoromethyl alkenes.

In Ni/photoredox coupling of the masked substrates, carbonate and other basic additives gave only partial conversion, whereas KF was identified as the most effective additive and enabled products in good yield.
The authors hypothesize that basic additives may suppress Ni/photoredox coupling by deprotonating the relatively acidic alpha-trifluoromethyl alcohol.

Lewis-basic sites impeded TMSOTf-mediated Peterson elimination: some substrates required super-stoichiometric TMSOTf or protonation of a basic site, while less-basic amines underwent elimination with catalytic TMSOTf. Direct Suzuki cross-coupling of potassium trifluoromethylvinyl trifluoroborate with multiple aryl and heteroaryl bromides was demonstrated using palladium and phosphine ligands, including functionalized and drug-like substrates; some substrates required variation of the phosphine ligand.

A sequential demonstration converted a trifluoromethyl alkene to a gem-difluoroalkene by radical defluorinative alkylation and later subjected a second trifluoromethyl alkene to another selective radical defluorinative alkylation, directly supporting selective single-defluorination of this alkene class in a carbon-radical manifold.

The 2-arylbenzimidazole scope tolerates varied electronic substitution, substitution positions, halogens, disubstituted and fused-ring substrates, a 2-thiophene group, substituted benzimidazole cores, and 2-arylimidazoles; meta-substituted substrates react at the less hindered C−H site with exclusive regioselectivity.

Scope limitations include lower efficacy with an NMe2-substituted benzimidazole, no reactivity for 2-(4-pyridyl)benzimidazole, and no desired products from 5-phenyl-1H-pyrazole, 2-phenyl-1H-indole, or 2-phenyl-1H-imidazo[4,5-c]pyridine.
The authors attribute the lack of reactivity of 2-(4-pyridyl)benzimidazole to strong coordination of its pyridine ring to the ruthenium catalyst.

The fluorinated diazoketone scope includes aryl and aliphatic substituents, fused rings, heterocycles, and cycloalkyl groups; halogen, trifluoromethyl, nitro, cyano, ketone, and ester groups were retained. The catalyst-screen reactions were conducted at 75 °C for 1 hour; the reported Rh/BF4 comparison used DCE at 120 °C for 24 hours.

All reported 1-(fluoromethylene)indan-2-one products were formed with greater than 95:5 E/Z selectivity by crude-mixture 19F NMR; the major configuration of 2c was established by single-crystal X-ray analysis and the remaining products were assigned by analogy.

A Lewis-basic ketone substituent reduced reactivity, which the authors attribute tentatively to competitive catalyst binding.

The method also furnished cyclopentanone 4 with 85:15 E/Z selectivity, six-membered heterocycles with yields and stereoselectivities comparable to prior RhI/BF4 catalysis, and tertiary fluoride 8 from a 1,1-disubstituted alkene in quantitative yield.

Catalytic activity depended strongly on both Lewis-acid identity and the BF4 counterion: changing BF4 to PF6 or BArF20 nearly stopped catalysis, while BCl3 and BBr3 produced halogen-exchange products.

Experiments disfavored a simple fluoride-abstraction pathway: a Friedel-Crafts probe gave only trace product with 81% recovery of the acyl fluoride, and catalytically relevant NMR experiments did not detect trityl fluoride.

The authors propose dual activation in which tritylium activates the acyl-fluoride carbonyl, BF4 supplies the initial fluoride, and collapse of a tetrahedral intermediate expels fluoride to regenerate TrBF4; cyclization and fluoride addition may be concerted or stepwise.

Changing the FeCl3 loading, solvent, or chloride source reduced the model defluorosulfonylation yield; omission of nBu4NCl reduced the yield to 56%.
The role of FeCl3 and light is qualitatively supported by the narrative, but the corresponding table entry is quantitatively ambiguous because it is reported as N.D. (not determined).
The defluorosulfonylation scope included polyfluoroarenes bearing cyano, acetyl, ester, and trifluoromethyl groups, as well as a heterocyclic polyfluoroarene.
Five-, eight-, and twelve-membered cycloalkanes furnished sulfonylated products with greater than 99:1 selectivity for substitution para to the cyano group.
Defluorinative alkylation coupled pentafluorobenzonitrile with cycloalkanes, adamantane, cyclic and linear ethers, alcohols, and amines in 43–83% yields, with substitution para to the cyano group.
The C(sp3)–H functionalization was position-selective: ethers reacted alpha to oxygen, alcohols at the alpha-oxy position, and N-aryl and N-Boc amines alpha to nitrogen.
Primary, secondary, tertiary, cyclic, and amino-acid-derived carboxylic acids participated in the defluorinative alkylation protocol.

For the alkane reaction, measured parallel and competitive kinetic isotope effects were 1.9 and 1.4, respectively; the authors interpreted these results as indicating that hydrogen-atom abstraction was not rate-determining.

The authors propose an LMCT pathway in which excited FeCl3 generates a chlorine radical, hydrogen-atom transfer forms an alkyl radical, radical addition to the polyfluoroarene is followed by single-electron reduction, and heterolytic C–F cleavage eliminates fluoride to form product.

The paper reports a one-pot synthesis of aryl perfluoroalkenyl ketones from perfluoroalkyl iodides and aroylsilanes by first converting the iodide to a perfluoroorganomagnesium bromide and then reacting it with the aroylsilane in ether at low temperature.

In method A, the perfluoroalkyl iodide is treated with ethylmagnesium bromide in ether at -45 °C for 0.5 h, followed by aroylsilane addition at -45 °C, warming to room temperature, triethylamine addition, and stirring for 2-4 h.

The optimized procedures furnished isolated E-configured aryl perfluoroalk-1-enyl ketones across several perfluoroalkyl and aryl substituents in reported yields of 83-95%; method A was not achieved for the C2F5/phenyl example, while method B gave that product in 91% yield.

Lithium-mediated conditions were difficult to control because the perfluoroalkyllithium was unstable and reacted rapidly; addition of methyllithium to already formed enone produced an alcohol byproduct.

Use of magnesium produced a more stable alcoholate intermediate; after 15 h at room temperature the enone was obtained cleanly without byproducts, and triethylamine substantially shortened the reaction time.

The authors propose a multistep mechanism in which nucleophilic addition is followed by a Brook rearrangement, beta-fluoride elimination to a perfluoroenoxysilane, and fluoride attack to form the enone; whether the final step is concerted or proceeds through an enolate was stated to be unresolved.

Evidence supporting an enoxysilane intermediate included isolation of a sterically hindered perfluoroenoxysilane and isolation of the hydrolysis product corresponding to the unisolated trimethylsilyl analogue.

The paper reports a [2 + 1]/[3 + 2]-cycloaddition sequence between terminal alkynes, difluorocarbene, and a diazo compound that provides 5-fluoropyridazines without isolation of intermediates.

Phenylacetylene was converted through 1-phenyl-2,2-difluorocyclopropene and then reacted with ethyl diazoacetate and triethylamine to afford fluoropyridazine 4aa in 77% overall yield as a single regioisomer.
Across the evaluated alkyne scope, expected 5-fluoropyridazines were obtained in 30-86% yield, including aryl alkynes with electron-donating or electron-withdrawing substituents.
A meta-CF3 aryl alkyne gave a modest 33% yield, while a para-NMe2 aryl alkyne underwent only degradation.

Lewis-basic heteroaromatic alkynes presented a compatibility boundary with difluorocarbene: 2-ethynylpyridine gave a low yield, and 3-ethynylpyridine underwent only degradation during difluorocyclopropenation.

Alkynes containing an sp3 nitrogen in imidazole or pyrazole decomposed with TMS-CF3, whereas protected piperidine and protected primary-amine substrates were compatible and furnished products in 63-73% yield.
软亲核试剂，如胺、醇、硫醇盐和稳定碳负离子，可取代所研究5-氟哒嗪的C5位氟，得到产物7a–f，收率从良好到定量。

Nucleophile hardness changed chemoselectivity: hard nucleophiles reacted with the C3 carbonyl group instead of displacing C5 fluorine, furnishing aldehyde, alcohol, amide, or ketone products.

The authors proposed that a dihydropyridazine intermediate would spontaneously aromatize by HF elimination and that the fused cyclopropanopyrazoline would readily expand because distal fluorine atoms weaken the fused bond.
The reported synthesis uses difluorofluorenes and acetoxyenone 15 to prepare dibenzochrysenes and diindenochrysenes, culminating in 5,6,11,12-tetrabromosemibuckminsterfullerene 31.
Biaryls 9 and 10 were formed by Suzuki coupling with reagent 8 in 98% and 96% yield, respectively.

Aryl groups were introduced by Suzuki reaction of derived enol triflates with commercially available arylboronic acids 18 or 19 because direct Grignard or aryllithium addition followed by dehydration produced a diene that did not undergo CuBr2 oxidative aromatization.
Under Amsharov's conditions, dibenzochrysene 26 gave diindenochrysene 28 in 84% yield, while 27 gave 29 in 80% yield.

The alumina-mediated C-F activation procedure failed for dibenzochrysenes bearing phenolic hydroxyl or phenolic methyl ether groups; the authors attribute this failure to preferential interaction of oxygen with the alumina surface, inhibiting C-C bond formation.
A prior mechanistic description assigns the alumina-mediated intramolecular dehydrofluorination to a dyotropic rearrangement driven by formation of a strong Al-F bond.

Octabromide 30 was generated by benzylic bromination and used without purification; refluxing it with aqueous sodium hydroxide in dioxane for 1.5 hours afforded semibuckminsterfullerene 31 in 40-60% overall yield across the two steps.
This paper is a review of methods for synthesizing indazole derivatives and of their biological activities, rather than a report focused on selective defluorinative coupling.

The review reports ligand-free palladium-catalyzed intramolecular C-H amination of aminohydrazones to form 1H-indazoles; the described transformation does not identify a trifluoroethyl carbonyl electrophile, organoboron partner, or selective defluorination.

The review reports SnCl2·H2O-mediated reductive cyclization to 3-perfluoroalkylated-2H-indazoles from an alpha-perfluoroalkylated benzylamine precursor; the cited text does not report selective C-F cleavage or formation of a monofluoroalkene.

A Cu/Pd cooperatively catalyzed tandem C-N/C-P bond-forming reaction of 2-alkynyl azobenzenes is reported to produce phosphorated 2H-indazoles in moderate to good yields with good functional-group tolerance.
For an iodine-mediated 2H-indazole synthesis, mechanistic studies suggested iodine-assisted hydrogen transfer, while DFT calculations were reported to support a radical-chain mechanism.
一种经合理设计的有机磷试剂通过 interrupted Perkow-type reaction，促使三氟甲基和五氟乙基酮中的一个 C−F 键被选择性转化，并允许以氯、溴或碘取代氟。
Monodefluorination generated an O-phosphorus enolate that underwent electrophilic halogenation to give α-chloro-, α-bromo-, and α-iodo-perfluoroalkyl ketones.

Polar sulfoxide conditions suppressed the competing aldol-type pathway: DMSO gave the best solvent outcome, and 1.5 equivalents of DMSO in CH2Cl2 was identified as optimal among the tested loadings.

Electron-rich p-anisyl trifluoromethyl ketone required modified conditions because defluorination was slow under the standard sulfoxide/CH2Cl2 conditions; complete consumption was achieved in DMF at 50 °C with excess phosphoramidite.
所展示的底物包括对卤代芳基、烯基、吲哚基和五氟乙基酮底物；其中吲哚基底物脱氟较慢，使用 5.0 当量试剂 1、在 50 °C 的 DMSO 中得到产物。
Alkyl ketone 2q underwent defluorination but no detectable halogenation; partial protonation occurred instead, and deliberate addition of water afforded protonated product 6q in 71% isolated yield.

Additional practical limitations included uncontrollable dimerization of an MFCA-derived reactant and instability of an electron-rich iodinated product that reduced its isolated yield.

The authors attribute improved formation of the desired intermediate in DMSO to stabilization of charge separation in the calculated rate-determining transition state, while the competing aldol pathway was calculated to have little solvent dependence.
Flash vacuum pyrolysis of hexafluoro-2,4-cyclohexadienone 3 at 625 °C and 0.1 torr produced hexafluorocyclopentadiene in 80% yield; the remaining material was nonvolatile.
The hexafluorocyclopentadiene product was identified by comparison of its IR, mass, and 19F NMR spectra with literature values and readily dimerized at room temperature.

The authors propose that pyrolysis of dienone 3 may proceed through electrocyclic ring opening to an alpha-fluoro ketene, decarbonylation to a carbene, and cyclization either directly or through hexafluorovinylcyclopropene; the cyclopropene intermediate was not observed and could not be ruled out.

The 2,5-dienone 4 was substantially less reactive than the 2,4-isomer: it gave only 10% hexafluorocyclopentadiene at 625 °C, while higher temperatures increased product formation but also increased unidentified impurities.

Preparative pyrolysis of a mixture of dienones 3 and 4 at 625 °C and 0.04 mm gave hexafluorocyclopentadiene in 53% isolated yield and 95% purity, with additional product and unreacted dienone 4 remaining in the pot.
Photochemical irradiation of dienone 4 at 254 nm produced unidentified products and no hexafluorocyclopentadiene.
For hexafluorocyclopentadiene 1, the authors state that nucleophilic attack tends to displace a vinyl fluorine by addition-elimination rather than a geminal fluorine by an SN2-prime or SN2 pathway.

Unreacted pentafluorophenol destroys the reactive 2,4-dienone 3 by addition-elimination, and attempts to remove the phenol with base, water, or bicarbonate accelerated or reproduced the unwanted condensation.

Excess fluorinating agent minimized formation of condensation product 6; prolonged contact of dienone 3 with trifluoromethyl hypofluorite converted 3 into tar, and elemental fluorine attacked sensitive dienone 3 as the reported 3:2 ratio increased.

Pyrolysis of dienone 13 at 550 °C gave chloropentafluorocyclopentadienes 15 and 16 in a 2.3:1 ratio, with no detected 5-chloro isomer 14; pyrolysis of isolated 15 gave the same 15/16 mixture, demonstrating equilibration under those conditions.

In an alternative ring-expansion route, bromotrifluoroethylene and tetrafluorocyclopropene gave 4- and 3-bromocyclopentenes in an 84:16 ratio, but only 31% purified yield; subsequent zinc/zinc chloride reduction in diglyme furnished hexafluorocyclopentadiene in 92% yield and 98% purity.

Anhydrous lithium hydroxide converted hexafluorotropone into pentafluorotropolone at room temperature in benzene, affording an approximately 85% pure product in 72% yield based on consumed hexafluorotropone.

The lithium hydroxide procedure favored pentafluorotropolone formation over the alternative hydroxy regioisomers: less than 10% of the 3-hydroxy derivative and none of the 4-hydroxy derivative were present.
The authors attribute the improved regioselectivity of the lithium hydroxide synthesis to coordination by the carbonyl group directing hydroxide attack toward neighboring carbons.

A previously reported aqueous sodium hydroxide procedure produced three hydroxy derivatives in 65% yield and a 15:65:20 ratio, with the 2-position described as the least favored site of hydroxide attack.
Hexafluorotropone is a very weak base; half protonation was observed at H0 = -6.2 ± 0.5, assigned as the pKa of its conjugate acid, approximately 100,000-fold lower in basicity than parent tropone.

The authors report nickel-catalyzed carbonylation of secondary trifluoromethylated alkyl iodides with arylboronic acids under 1 atm of CO.
The reported condition development identified NiBr2·DME, L2, K2CO3, and dioxane as the productive catalyst system; using 5 mol% NiBr2·DME and 6 mol% L2 gave 3b in 70% isolated yield.
Control reactions lacking either nickel or ligand did not provide the desired product.

Both electron-rich and electron-deficient arylboronic acids reacted, and the reported partner scope tolerated amine, morpholine, thioether, ester, enolizable ketone, silyl, furan, thiophene, dibenzofuran, and ortho-methyl substitution.

The electrophile scope included trifluoromethylated secondary alkyl iodides and extended to difluoromethylated and difluoroacetylated secondary alkyl iodides; alkene, cyclopropanecarboxylic ester, and amino-acid-derived substrates were reported as suitable.
Under the reported conditions, the tested unactivated secondary aliphatic iodide 2-iodobutane afforded the corresponding product in less than 10% yield.
The authors attribute the higher competence of the trifluoromethylated alkyl iodide to the electron-withdrawing CF3 group making electron acceptance easier than for the nonfluorinated analogue.

The authors proposed that transmetalation could generate a nickel-nucleophile species, followed by CO insertion and formal oxidative addition of the trifluoromethylated alkyl iodide; reductive elimination from the resulting high-valent nickel species was proposed to produce the product while suppressing beta-fluoride elimination.

In stoichiometric experiments, an arylnickel complex reacted with CO to give an acylnickel complex in 71% yield, and treatment of that complex with the trifluoromethylated secondary alkyl iodide afforded ketone 3a in 52% yield without observation of the beta-fluoride-elimination byproduct.
Radical-scavenger experiments diminished ketone formation, and a radical-clock experiment afforded a ring-opened product in 23% yield together with 6% coupling product.
Zero or low phenolic acid surrogate recoveries were occasionally observed in natural-water samples, and the low recoveries were usually attributed to oxidation during acid extraction.

Three oxidation products were detected for the phenolic acid surrogates; benzoquinone-d4 and fluorobenzoquinone were assigned as products of phenol-d5 and 2-fluorophenol, while the product from 2,4,6-tribromophenol was only tentatively identified as 2,6-dibromohydroquinone.

The identified products accounted for only a small fraction of the lost surrogates; the authors proposed formation of acid-soluble, nonextractable, nonvolatile, or polymeric oxidation products as possible explanations.
Low recoveries were obtained for the listed phenols bearing electron-releasing substituents or weaker electron-withdrawing substituents under the reported sample conditions.
For 2,4-dimethylphenol, recovery depended strongly on extraction pH: only 2.6% was recovered at pH 7, whereas initial extraction at pH 10 gave high recovery in the presence of oxidizing agents.
Correlation, EDTA, and ICP results led the authors to identify manganese(III,IV) oxides as the most likely phenol oxidants, but the causal assignment remained qualified rather than definitive.
Changing the order of extraction so that acidic extraction preceded alkaline extraction gave good recoveries for all tested phenols.

The authors proposed that alkaline extraction and exposure to air convert dissolved Mn(II) to manganese(III,IV) oxides, which then oxidize medium- and weak-acidity phenols during the subsequent acidic extraction.

The reported oxidation problem could be eliminated by adding sodium thiosulfate before extraction, or by extraction at pH <2 alone or initial extraction at pH 2 followed by pH >11, provided manganese(III,IV) oxide particulates were not present before acid extraction; sodium thiosulfate occasionally produced large amounts of S8 under strongly acidic conditions.

The reported transformation is a palladium-catalyzed alkylation of electron-deficient polyfluoroarenes through a domino Heck/intermolecular C−H bond-functionalization pathway involving transient alkylpalladium(II) intermediates.
For the model reaction, SPhos outperformed PPh3, XPhos, Xantphos, and DPEphos and gave product 3a in 71% yield.
A base was required for effective conversion, and K2CO3 performed better than Cs2CO3, LiOtBu, KOtBu, and Et3N in the reported screen.
The solvent composition materially affected the reaction: EtOAc/H2O at 2:1 gave the highest isolated yield of 89%, whereas pure water gave 21%.
